belongs_to: Date trick: 'Let us now look at a different trick of this type' / 'How did Shubham figure out the date chosen by Mukta?'
description: Three-panel comic of Shubham (boy, teal shirt, curly hair, left) and Mukta (girl, yellow top, pigtail, right). Panel 1 (yellow background, black rounded frame): Shubham's four speech bubbles stacked in a column, top to bottom: 'Think of a date.', 'Multiply the month by 5.', 'Add 6.', 'Multiply by 4.' Mukta (thinking, arms folded) has a chain of six oval thought bubbles climbing down the right side, top to bottom: '26/01', '1 × 5 = 5', '5 + 6 = 11', '11 × 4 = 44', '44 + 9 = 53', '53 × 5 = 265' (the last two bubbles lie beside panel 2). Panel 2 (no frame, white background): Shubham with closed eyes, three bubbles stacked: 'Add 9.', 'Multiply by 5.', 'Add the day.'; a fourth bubble below them: 'Tell me your answer.' Mukta, hand on chin, beside the thought-bubble chain. Panel 3 (pale green background, black rounded frame): Mukta's oval speech bubble '265 + 26 = 291.' (tail points to her) and Shubham's bubble at the bottom 'You thought of our Republic Day, 26/01.' So the picture carries the 6 calculation steps with the numbers for the date 26/01 (month 1, day 26) and the reported answer 291.
unclear: Speaker of '265 + 26 = 291.' taken as Mukta from the direction of the bubble tail; the characters' names Shubham and Mukta come from the text, not from labels in the picture.

belongs_to: 6.6 Decoding Divisibility Tricks: 'It is now Mukta's turn to show a mathematics trick to Shubham.' (Choose a 2-digit number ... 47, 74, 74 - 47 = 27, 27/9 = 3)
description: Two-panel comic of Mukta (girl, yellow top, curly hair, left) and Shubham (boy, teal shirt, right). Panel 1 (pale green background, rounded frame): Mukta's four speech bubbles stacked, top to bottom: 'Choose a 2-digit number of different digits and don't reveal it!', 'Reverse the digits to get another number.', 'Find their difference.', 'Divide the result by 9.' Shubham (hand on chin) has four cloud-shaped thought bubbles down the right side, top to bottom: '47', '74', '74 – 47 = 27', and '27/9 = 3' (the last written as a fraction, 27 over 9, equals 3). Panel 2 (pale yellow background, rounded frame): Mukta says 'There won't be any remainder.'; Shubham (looking surprised) says 'Yes, you are right. But how did you know?' So the picture carries the 4 steps worked on the number 47.
